I improved understandability by stripping the test down to only what it exercises — the `lengthOfYear()` check on December 31 — while keeping identical behavior:

- **Removed dead code**: deleted the 12 unused data-provider methods (`data_samples`, `data_with`, `data_until`, etc.) and ~50 unused imports that obscured the single test's purpose.
- **Readable data**: replaced the dense one-line `Object[][]` with one `Arguments.of(...)` per line, grouped by calendar era (Julian / 1752 cutover / Gregorian) with comments explaining *why* each leap-year rule produces the expected length. All 26 entries are preserved in their original order, including duplicates.
- **Clear naming & docs**: descriptive parameter name (`expectedLength`), a named local (`lastDayOfYear`), and a class-level Javadoc explaining the British cutover context.

The same call — `BritishCutoverDate.of(year, 12, 31).lengthOfYear()` — runs against the same 26 argument pairs with the same expected results.
